claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising an fcc matrix and hexagonal C14 Laves precipitates.
The fcc matrix in the FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at about 100 Oe because their orbital moments are insufficient.
The intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase remains limited when C14 coexists with it.
The fcc/C14 interface establishes strong antiferromagnetic exchange coupling in FeCoNiTi.
Hybridization between Ti 3d states in C14 and Fe/Co 3d states in fcc mediates the proposed interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling.
Antiferromagnetic coupling at the interface creates a local magnetic dead layer and suppresses saturation magnetization.
The fcc/C14 phase boundary pins domain walls and creates a high-energy barrier to domain-wall motion.
Local strain arising from fcc/C14 lattice mismatch increases effective magnetic anisotropy.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling, domain-wall pinning, and strain-induced anisotropy enable coercivity above the nominal 100 Oe fcc limit.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will exhibit coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
A single-phase fcc FeCoNi control will remain below 100 Oe at 400 K.
A C14-dominant alloy will exhibit a distinct lower-temperature magnetic transition attributable to the C14 phase.
A C14-dominant alloy will have lower overall saturation magnetization than the fcc phase alone.
The proposed mechanism requires thermodynamically stable C14 precipitates with coherent or semi-coherent interfaces to the fcc matrix.
The mechanism may not operate if the C14 phase is amorphous or its interface with fcc is incoherent.

A spin-polarized DFT supercell containing an explicit fcc/C14 interface can compare the element-resolved density of states at the Fermi level and the relative stability of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.

Comparing temperature-dependent magnetization and hysteresis among dual-phase, C14-dominant, and single-phase fcc alloys can isolate phase-specific transitions and test whether coercivity scales with C14 volume fraction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mediator assert strong antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling, while the uncertainty field states that even the sign of the coupling—ferromagnetic versus antiferromagnetic—is not definitively known.
